title: One object through the Ceph stack
summary: Follow a write from an S3 client through RGW and RADOS to OSD disks.

steps.n: The client sends an S3 PUT request to an RGW daemon.
RGW has a current map of monitors, OSDs and rules from the monitors.
RGW writes the object into a pool in RADOS using librados.
The object is hashed to a placement group and sent to the primary OSD.
The primary writes locally and forwards the data to the replica OSDs.
After all copies are safe the OSD acknowledges and RGW returns success.

title: Failure and recovery: losing a monitor majority
summary: Two monitors fail in the same rack and the cluster stops until quorum returns.

steps.n: Clients ask the monitors for the map and the three monitors agree.
Monitors B and C share a rack, and both lose power.
Monitor A alone cannot form a majority and refuses to commit changes.
Clients cannot get an updated map, and applications see hung storage.
The operator sees one of three monitors up and no quorum in ceph status.
Power is restored to the rack and the monitors start again.
Monitors B and C rejoin, a majority forms, and IO resumes.
The operator redeploys monitors across three racks so one failure never removes the majority.

title: From object name to OSDs
summary: Hash an object to a placement group and let CRUSH choose OSDs.

steps.n: The client names the pool and the object invoice-42.
The name is hashed, giving placement group 7.3 in the pool.
The client computes which OSDs hold PG 7.3 using the CRUSH rule.
The rule picks three OSDs on three different hosts.
The client sends the write to the first OSD, which acts as primary.
The primary replicates to the other two, so a host failure loses at most one copy.

title: Bootstrapping and growing a cluster
summary: Create the first node, add hosts and let the orchestrator create OSDs.

steps.n: The admin runs cephadm bootstrap on the first host with its monitor IP.
The bootstrap creates a monitor, a manager and the orchestrator module.
The admin adds a second host with ceph orch host add.
The orchestrator deploys monitor and OSD containers according to labels.
It scans hosts for empty devices that match the OSD service rule.
New OSDs are created on the free disks and join the cluster.

title: A PVC becomes an RBD image
summary: ceph-csi turns a Kubernetes volume claim into an image in a pool.

steps.n: A pod asks for a PVC that uses the ceph-rbd StorageClass.
The external provisioner calls the ceph-csi controller.
ceph-csi creates a thin provisioned RBD image of the requested size.
The image is striped across objects in a replicated pool.
On the node the image is mapped as a block device and mounted into the pod.
The pod writes data, and the image uses space only as blocks are written.

title: Reading a file on CephFS
summary: The client asks the MDS for metadata and reads data directly from OSDs.

steps.n: The client sends the path to the active MDS.
The MDS reads or caches the inode and layout from the metadata pool.
It returns the file layout and gives the client rights to cache and read.
The client reads the file objects from the data pool without going through the MDS.
The active MDS crashes while serving other clients.
A standby MDS replays the journal and becomes active within seconds.

title: A bucket listing that slows down
summary: An oversized bucket index is resharded to restore listing speed.

steps.n: The application lists a very large bucket through the load balancer.
The balancer forwards the request to a healthy RGW daemon.
RGW reads the bucket index, which sits in a single shard.
With hundreds of millions of objects one shard is huge, so listing is slow.
RGW cannot answer in time and the application times out.
The operator reshards the bucket to many shards, and dynamic resharding is enabled.

title: Failure and recovery: draining storage nodes too quickly
summary: Draining a second node before recovery finishes leaves data with one copy.

steps.n: The operator drains storage node 1 for maintenance.
The PGs on node 1 lose a copy and Ceph starts recovery to other OSDs.
Without checking health, the operator drains node 2 as well.
Some PGs have lost two of three copies and fall below min_size.
Those PGs go inactive, and the application sees hung volumes.
The toolbox shows inactive PGs and the two drained nodes.
The operator uncordons node 2 so its OSDs return.
PGs become active again, and the team waits for HEALTH_OK between drains.

title: Writing an object to an EC 4+2 pool
summary: Split an object into four data chunks and two coding chunks.

steps.n: The client sends a 4 MB object to the primary OSD of the placement group.
The primary splits it into four data chunks of 1 MB.
It computes two coding chunks of 1 MB from the data.
Each chunk goes to a different host, giving six hosts in use.
Two hosts holding chunks fail at the same time.
The remaining four chunks rebuild the object, so reads still succeed.

title: A replicated write on the network
summary: Trace a write across the public and cluster networks.

steps.n: The client sends the write over the public network.
The primary OSD receives the data and writes it to its WAL.
The primary sends the data to two replicas over the cluster network.
Each replica writes to its own device and acknowledges.
Both acknowledgements arrive at the primary.
The primary acknowledges once all copies are safe, so latency follows the slowest replica.

title: Failure and recovery: replacing a failed disk
summary: An OSD fails and a new disk is added without losing data.

steps.n: The disk behind OSD 12 stops responding.
Monitors mark OSD 12 down after missed heartbeats.
Its PGs run with two copies and keep serving IO.
After the timeout the monitors mark OSD 12 out and start recovery.
Other OSDs create the missing third copies on different hosts.
The operator removes OSD 12 and adds a new disk as a new OSD.
Data flows onto the new OSD in the background.
ceph status shows HEALTH_OK, and the operator moves on to the next task.

title: An orchestrated upgrade
summary: cephadm upgrades daemons in a safe order, waiting for health between steps.

steps.n: The operator starts an upgrade to a target Ceph version.
The orchestrator replaces monitors one at a time and waits for quorum.
It then upgrades managers while a standby stays available.
OSDs are restarted in small groups, with checks that PGs stay active.
Metadata and gateway daemons are upgraded last.
The status shows all daemons on the new version and the cluster HEALTH_OK.
